articleTitle: FCN Based Gas Leakage Segmentation and Improvement Using Transfer Learning
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS 2019)
abstract: This paper explores the usage of a fully convolutional network (FCN) to segment gas leakage images for gas detection. Quality management and safety control is an integral part in preserving workplace safety. This is especially true if the workplace deals with hazardous and dangerous materials, such natural-gas processing plant and chemical plant. In such working environment, one of the safety measures that can be taken is by having early detection of any possible leak. This paper tries to use the images of gas leak from thermal camera to train a semantic segmentation network to classify regions with gas leakage. Since the dataset requires videos recorded using thermal camera of gas leakage, collecting real life data has its own barriers (safety reason, availability, etc.). To help supplement the lack of available data, transfer learning were performed using smoke video which share similar characteristics with the gas leakage visually.

articleTitle: OCR for Drawing Images Using Bidirectional LSTM with CTC
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS 2019)
abstract: Nowadays, the system is changing with the Optical Character Recognition (OCR) technology in various industrial. It is technology that allows computers detect and convert form handwritten or scanned images into searchable machine encoded data. Searchable data can save a huge amount of time and effort. Therefore, the machine industry has also improved portability and accessibility by converting existing dealer customers' mechanical parts drawing books into mobile. Dealers can easily order mechanical parts without looking for drawing, just search a serial number of mechanical parts on the database. In this paper, we propose the OCR on the drawing images to convert images into searchable data. Proposed OCR consist of three parts: pre-processing, deep learning and postprocessing. The pre-processing part removed the guide lines and shape for improving the precision. The guide lines and shape usually cause false recognition as `1' or `7'. The deep learning part extract features and classify the images. We adopt Shi, et al.'s CRNN architecture [1]. The post-processing, drop the low probability of object. Most of left lines and shapes are seem to the low probability. As result of proposed OCR, it shows 98.52% of average recall rate and 92.25% average precision.

articleTitle: A Switching Method for Improving Lifetime of DC-Link Capacitors in Hybrid ANPC Inverters
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS 2019)
abstract: This paper presents a switching strategy for improving lifetime of DC-link capacitors in photovoltaic (PV) hybrid active neutral-point-clamped (ANPC) inverters. The DC-link capacitor current ripples should be reduced, because the high current ripples of the capacitors cause high thermal stress and short lifetime of the capacitors. To reduce the DC-link current ripples, the switching sequence of the conventional space vector pulse width modulation (SVPWM) method is replaced with the proposed switching sequence. By applying the proposed method, the DC-link current ripples are reduced substantially. The effectiveness of the proposed method was verified by simulation results.

articleTitle: Design of Spider-type Non-Destructive Testing Device Using Magnetic Flux Leakage
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS 2019)
abstract: The Magnetic Flux Leakage (MFL) method is a Non-Destructive Testing (NDT) that detects defects by using Pipeline Inspection Gauge (PIG) to detect MFL when passing through a defective area. Using these principles, this paper studied the design of mobile small PIG that can operate in piping perpendicular to the ground. Unlike the conventional PIG, a spider-type mobile small-scale design was designed to be attached to vertical piping and operable. It was analyzed using 3D Finite Element Method (FEM) and measured and analyzed data through experimentation. It was analyzed using a method, measured and analyzed data through manufacturing and experiment.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of BLDC Motor for Improving Regenerative Characteristics in Personal Mobility
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS 2019)
abstract: Increase the back emf of the BLDC motor for regenerative braking to be used for personal mobility. Promotion is based on the principle of electromagnetic induction. In addition, the data values are analyzed through finite element analysis (FEA).

articleTitle: Open-Switch Fault Detection for Hybrid ANPC Inverter Based on Current Distortion
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS 2019)
abstract: In this paper, an open-switch fault detection method is proposed for a hybrid active neutral-point clamped (ANPC) inverter. The hybrid ANPC topology used 4 silicon switches and 2 silicon carbide switches to generate the three-level output voltage. The open-switch fault in the hybrid ANPC inverter leads to a distortion of the output current. The current distortion decreases efficiency and eventually breaks down the system. Therefore, an open-switch fault detection method is required to improve the reliability of the hybrid ANPC inverter. Radius and angle in the dq-axis determine the location of the faulty switch. This method identifies the faulty switch without using additional sensors. Simulation results verified the validity of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Direct Torque Control of IM Fed by 3L-NPC Inverter with Simple Flux Regulation Technique
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS 2019)
abstract: Classical direct torque control (DTC) is considered one of the simplest and fastest control algorithm in motor drives. However, it produces high torque and flux ripples. Moreover, it loses its robustness when driving induction motor (IM) at very low-speed region. Replacing the conventional three-level hysteresis torque regulator (HTR) by five-level HTR for three-level neutral-point clamped (3L-NPC) inverter reduces the torque and flux ripples in DTC drives. Nevertheless, the stator flux is unregulated at very low-speed of IM where the domination of stator resistance is high. This problem causes the stator current to be highly distorted. To alleviate this problem, a simple flux regulation method is applied for low-speed operation of IM fed by 3L-NPC inverter. The proposed flux regulation algorithm modifies the output status of the five-level HTR depending on flux error, torque error and stator flux position. It first detects the direction of stator flux vector and which sector has been affected by flux-droop, and then it modifies the five-level HTR status to eliminate the usage of zero voltage vector for that particular effected sector only. This method stabilizes stator flux for both forward and reverse rotational directions of IM with retaining the basic structure of classical DTC. By using the proposed algorithm, the stator flux is regulated hence pure sinusoidal current waveform is achieved which results in lower total harmonics distortion (THD). Simulation results show the effectiveness of the proposed flux regulation method.

articleTitle: Finite Element Analysis and Optimal Design of DC Brush Motor for Automotive Engine Start Applications
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS 2019)
abstract: The purpose of this paper is to study the DC brush motor used in automobile engines. In the research, the diesel generator starting motor of the 4-pole 21-slot internal structure is used as the reference object prototype. The finite element magnetic circuit analysis software, RMxprt and Maxwell 2D by ANSYS, are used to modeling and analyze the transient magnetic field characteristics in a parametric manner. The electrical and magnetic characteristics including induced electromotive force, armature current, electromagnetic torque, rated speed, magnetic flux density and magnetic field distribution of the magnetic circuit are discussed. With the geometric dimensions of the reference motor, different stator and rotor core materials, the finite element analysis software RMxprt is used to quickly establish a DC brushed motor model. The results of the RMxprt were analyzed by two-dimensional finite element analysis software Maxwell 2D. Two improvement schemes are proposed to optimize the pole core. One is to cut the pole core into two parts, using different materials as the pole core, which can reduce the magnetic saturation phenomenon at the tip of the pole core. The second way is digging holes in the front pole tip forced the magnetic distribution toward to the rear pole tip for improving the magnetic saturation phenomenon. In the paper, the optimal design of the hole in the front pole of the pole core was selected. The stator structure was optimized by the Taguchi algorithm for maximum output power. At the rated speed of 3,400 rpm, the output torque after the reducer was 73.44 N-m, the output power can be as high as 7.69 kW, verified the feasibility of the improvement strategy.

articleTitle: An Improved Position Control of PMSM Considering Vibration
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS 2019)
abstract: This paper proposed to reduce the position error caused by vibration in the use of PMSMs (Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motors) for specific applications. In order to improve the accuracy of the position control, an accurate information of the rotor is mandatory and proper current control is necessary to apply load to the motor. Most vibration occurs in the acceleration and deceleration sections, so proper control is required in these sections to reduce vibration. In this paper, to reduce the vibration in the acceleration and deceleration sections, various acceleration/deceleration patterns are proposed and current control methods according to load are also proposed. The proposed method improved the position control performance and it was validated by simulation and experiments.

articleTitle: A Novel Circuit of Power Converters applied to EV Wireless Charging System
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS 2019)
abstract: A circuit topology of power converters with high frequency and high output power characteristics for electric vehicle (EV) magnetically-coupled resonant wireless power charging system is proposed in this paper. The rectifier of this circuit provides less harmonic pollution to the power grid compared to traditional rectifiers. At the same time the inverter of this circuit achieves higher output power than the bridge inverter under the same DC voltage input condition. A Matlab/Simulink model is built and the simulations are carried out. The results verify the effectiveness of the circuit.

articleTitle: A Loss Calculation Method of Motor Stator Core Excited by Harmonic Magnetic Field Based on Multiscale Energy Model
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS 2019)
abstract: The presence of harmonic components in the excitation will increase iron core losses in electrical machines and it is significant to compute core loss accurately for the optimal design of high power density motors. In this paper, a hysteresis model based on the minimization of magnetic domain energy is developed to describe the vector relationship between the magnetization M and magnetic field strength H under harmonic magnetic fields. After that, the stator core loss distribution of an electrical machine is calculated by the integral of dM/dt and H as stated by the Poynting's theorem. The effectiveness of loss calculation method proposed here is also verified by the experimental data.

articleTitle: Comparisons of Permanent-Magnet Machines with Different Rotor Topologies for Quadruped Robot
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS 2019)
abstract: For quadruped robot, permanent-magnet (PM) machines are competitive due to their promising high torque density. In this paper, four PM motors with fractional-slot concentrated windings (FSCW) are designed and compared. They are designed with the same design specifications but different rotor topologies, including surface-mounted PM (SPM), flat-shape interior PM (F-IPM), V-shape interior PM (V-IPM) and consequent-pole (CP). Electromagnetic performances of these motors are analyzed using finite element method (FEM) and the main concern of this comparison is the electromagnetic torque characteristic. It is proved that SPMSM achieves the highest electromagnetic torque and CP PM motor may become a new option for quadruped robot owing to the better torque performance and less PM material usage compared with IPMSM.

articleTitle: Zero Voltage Vector - Based Predictive Direct Torque Control for PMSM
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS 2019)
abstract: In this paper, we proposed a zero voltage vector-based PDTC-PWM (Predictive Direct Torque Control - Pulse Width Modulation) control method of PMSM. DTC selects the voltage vectors from the flux and torque errors. However, these vectors may not satisfy both torque response and motor speed requirements due to back EMF and decoupling effects. Therefore, back EMF and decoupling components should be considered in the voltage vector selection to improve the control performance of PMSM. The proposed zero voltage vector - based PDTC-PWM predicts the flux and torque of the next sample. It is then used to calculate the output voltage vector and the optimal PWM duty ratio based on the error value between the command value and the predicted value of the flux and torque. Simulation results show that the proposed zero voltage vector based - PDTC-PWM control method for PMSM provides excellent control performance with low torque ripple.

articleTitle: Radial Force Reduction of Switched Reluctance Motor with Inner Rotor Holes
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS 2019)
abstract: In this paper, a novel rotor structure that implements holes within the rotor of a switched reluctance motor (SRM) to reduce the radial force while maintaining the output torque is proposed. Radial force contributes to vibration in SRM, especially because of its doubly salient, single excited structure. The effect of holes in the rotor is examined in this study. Finite element analysis (FEA) is used to see the characteristics of the motor. Simulation results show the viability of the proposed structure.

articleTitle: Adaptive Virtual Impedance Control Method for Accurate Reactive Power Sharing and Circulating Current Suppression in Islanded Microgrid
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS 2019)
abstract: In a practical microgrid, a feeder impedance mismatch increases the reactive power sharing error and circulating current among distributed generation units (DGs). This paper proposes an adaptive virtual impedance control method to improve reactive power sharing accuracy and suppress the circulating current. To achieve the control objective, the virtual impedance is added to the DG output to compensate for the mismatched feeder impedance among DGs. In addition, the proposed controller maintains a good power sharing performance despite the load changes. The effectiveness of the proposed adaptive virtual impedance control method is evaluated with PLECS simulation results.

articleTitle: Modeling of Anisotropic Magnetic Property in Motor Stator Cores Using Vector Play Model
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS 2019)
abstract: The study shows that even non-oriented electrical steel sheets have strongly anisotropic magnetic characteristics. Accurate modeling of magnetic properties of core materials is of importance for improving motor performance and reducing energy consumption. In this paper, a vector play model is improved to describe anisotropic magnetic properties of electrical steel sheet based on experimental test, in which the vector shape function is expressed as the vector addition of those along two orthogonal direction, and its effectiveness is verified by experimental data. Finally, the proposed model is applied to simulate magnetic hysteresis loop distributions in local regions of stator core of an electrical machine.

articleTitle: Color Scheme of PWM Vector Control for 3-Phase AC Machines
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS 2019)
abstract: The purpose of this paper is to describe the PWM voltage vectors of the 3-phase AC motor drives with RGB color code, realize the color scheme for the vector control, so as to provide a new and visible approach to understanding the vector control principle. RGB color code can be regarded as a set of three-phase coordinate values and it forms a color vector, which is consistent with the vector addition rule. When a variable in the motor vector control is represented with a set of three-phase coordinate values, after adding the corresponding zero sequence components and multiplying the corresponding coefficient, it corresponds to RGB color code. When the three-phase to two-phase coordinate transformation with the color code is realized, the specific location on the plane where the color vector locates is obtained. In this way, the correspondence between the motor vector control variable, the RGB color code and the location on the plane is achieved. Then, the color change process on the plane visualizes the three-phase AC motor PWM vector control process.
